text:
Lina (support): @here AcmeCorp reporting repeated 504s to hosted inference between ~11:02–11:12 UTC. Customer says requests time out and their frontend shows gateway 504s. I have ticket #INC-4821. Logs show spikes of 5xx from our gateway.
Raj (sre): Can you paste the gateway traces and any scale events? Did HPA/KEDA report scaling activity? :rotating_light:
Lina (support): Gateway trace: most requests got proxied to model-service and then hung until timeout. Short excerpt:
```
[11:03:12] gateway -> model-svc: started request
[11:03:12] model-svc: queuing, waiting for pod
[11:03:20] gateway: timeout -> 504
```
We saw a pileup, not consistent application errors.
Mike (infra): Pulled cluster events and pod status for tenant namespace. Looks like pods stuck Pending/ImagePull issues and node autoscaler retries. Snippets:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n acme
NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
model-svc-7654f7b8c-zz9p               0/1     Pending   0          3m

$ kubectl describe pod model-svc-7654f7b8c-zz9p -n acme
Events:
  Type     Reason               Age                From               Message
  ----     ------               ----               ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling     3m (x12 over 4m)   default-scheduler  0/0 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu
  Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox 2m (x3 over 3m)  kubelet            failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull image: unauthorized: authentication required
```
Mike (infra): Also saw node pool autoscaler errors when trying to create nodes: provider API returned 403/429 in short bursts. Full cloud logs attached to ticket.
Elaine (prod): Looking at control plane logs, there was a billing enforcement action for the tenant that kicked in at 11:00 UTC — our billing service temporarily put tenant into a quota-throttle state due to a payment processing delay. That caused our infra to reject some provisioning API calls (403) to the external node provider for that tenant's reserved capacity. Chain looks like: billing throttle -> node creation rejected -> pods pending -> KEDA/HPA kept scaling requests -> gateway timeouts.
Raj (sre): That explains why HPA kept increasing desired replicas but pods never landed. KEDA ScaledObject shows rapid scale signals (queueLength spikes) and a short cooldown (30s). It tried to create pods repeatedly, but the node creation failed. Also image pull auth errors indicate our registry token rotated at ~10:58 and some agent didn't refresh quickly.
AutoscaleBot: Alert: scaledobject acme-model-svc hit maxScaleAttempt=5 between 11:03:00-11:05:00; cooldown=30s. (autoscale-controller)
Lina (support): Customer impacted production requests for ~10 minutes. They've asked for root cause and ETA. Any quick mitigations we can apply now?
Mike (infra): Short-term mitigations:
- Manually add a small pre-warm node to the cluster for multitenant fallback (requires override of billing-quota, will need buy-in from billing)
- Temporarily route AcmeCorp traffic to a smaller model variant (less CPU/memory) to land on existing nodes
- Retry image pull by forcing token refresh on kubelets in affected zones

Elaine (prod): Ops path:
1) Pause billing enforcement for tenant for 30m to allow node provisioning to succeed (billing team confirmed they can whitelist)
2) Increase KEDA scaledobject cooldown to 120s to avoid thrashing once nodes come up
3) Bump readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds from 5 -> 30 for model container so gateway waits for warmup instead of instant probe fail

Raj (sre): Also recommend adding a prewarm pool (2 small pods) pinned for high-SLA tenants to avoid end-to-end 504s on cold bursts.
Lina (support): I'll propose credits and explain the remediation steps to AcmeCorp. They accepted temporary route to smaller model for immediate relief.
Mike (infra): Executed kubelet token refresh on 2/3 nodes; verified image pulls succeeding now. Also cloud provider accepted node create after billing whitelist pushed at 11:10 UTC.
Raj (sre): Pods now scheduling and becoming Ready; model logs show init sequence ~11:12–11:15. Gateway 504 rate dropped to baseline after 11:16.
Lina (support): Customer notified, accepted interim mitigation and requested postmortem + timeline for permanent fix. They've asked for SLA credit estimate.
Elaine (prod): Owners: infra=Mike, sre=Raj, product=Elaine, support=Lina. I'll open INC-4821-PM for postmortem and link runbook.
Raj (sre): Action items for follow-up:
- (Raj) Postmortem with timeline and RCA (billing throttle + image token rotation + KEDA cooldown)
- (Mike) Ensure registry token rollout has kubelet refresh hook
- (Elaine) Product to propose prewarm pool for high-SLA tenants + policy for billing whitelist on transient payment issues
- (Lina) Coordinate customer credits and communications

Lina (support): Thanks team. I’ll keep the ticket updated and close the incident once PM doc is linked. :thumbsup:
Mike (infra): Good catch everyone. Will add a short diagnostic in the autoscale runbook to check billing throttle as early indicator.
Raj (sre): Adding a short query to our alerting: if scaledobject > attempts and pod Pending > 1m -> pager oncall for possible provisioning block.
Lina (support): Closing loop with customer now. :wave:
